transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Samara (CEO), Diego (CTO), Maya (Product), Jules (Eng), Priya (Research), Rohan (People), plus company-wide all-hands dial-in

Summary:
This all-hands focused on short-term experiments to improve cost/latency across hosted and dedicated tiers, a hiring snapshot, and a short Q&A about incident response and rollout guardrails. Leadership emphasized pragmatic experimentation over big rewrites and asked squads to treat a set of A/Bs as the canonical signal for December tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Experimentation framework & expected metrics
- Canary/rollback playbook and SLO guardrails
- Hiring freeze lift and IC leveling adjustments
- Research update on quantized model regressions
- People ops: benefits + holiday schedule reminder

Action items (covered above): see next_steps/action_items fields.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samara: All right good afternoon everyone, um thank you for joining, we'll keep this tight, we have a lot to cover but some quick updates, start with product and experiments.
[00:00:18] Maya: Hey team, quick context first — last quarter we shipped the continuous batching prototype to a subset of hosted customers, and the early signal is around a 12% token cost reduction on stable traffic but with a latency tail that popped on spikes, so we have three experiments starting next week to hedge that.
[00:00:42] Jules: yeah and to add, the canary showed a KV cache miss pattern that we didn't expect, so engineers adjusted cache priming logic overnight, but we want to run the A/B across both dedicated and hosted traffic to see cross-tenant effects.
[00:01:05] Diego: when you say KV cash — sorry — KV cache misses, are we confident that's instrumentation, or real eviction behavior?
[00:01:14] Jules: it's real at the 99th percentiles; our traces show the cache eviction correlates with some long sequences from a single customer. instrumentation is fine but the pattern is genuine.
[00:01:28] Samara: so that means the mitigation is both kernel-level handling and a routing policy tweak, correct?
[00:01:35] Jules: correct. we have a dual path: kernel fix for longer-term and routing policy to limit bursty tenants to variant B while they stabilize.
[00:01:47] Maya: experiment A is continuous batching + existing routing, B is batching + stricter tenant isolation, C is baseline with smarter prefix caching. We'll measure cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, and correctness regressions on our evaluation suite.
[00:02:06] [00:02:06] Priya: on the quality side, Research will run the regression harness against a curated prompt set — note there are some micro-flips on instruction-following for the quantized variants, we've seen few hallucination shifts when we switch quant profiles. not massive but measurable.
[00:02:24] Samara: okay please be explicit about the acceptable delta for quality — we don't want token savings that break product contracts.
[00:02:32] Priya: agreed — propose we set a 0.5% maximum drop in our core instruction pass-rate for the primary production cohort. if we hit that we pause the experiment.
[00:02:44] Diego: I want to call out operational cost of experiments — running A/B at production scale increases infra runway but reduces long-term unit cost. we should have finance run a quick look at burn vs expected savings so we can prioritize.
[00:03:00] Rohan: hiring note — we said we'd brief org this week: we are not re-freezing hiring, instead targeted roles will open: infra SRE, two backend, and one product manager for the Optimize toolkit. managers please post reqs by end of week.
[00:03:16] Samara: good. also a short reminder on leveling and IC compensation — we'll publish an FAQ in two days.
[00:03:24] [00:03:24] Audience question (Speaker 1): hi, is the experiment going to affect the SLA for our Dedicated customers or will they be opted out?
[00:03:34] Diego: Dedicated customers won't be mass-exposed to the A/B unless they opt in; we will run A/B on a mix of hosted and non-production traffic and a small percentage of dedicated if customers agree to partner in the pilot.
[00:03:47] Maya: and for committed accounts we'll respect capacity pins; canary will not override their model pins.
[00:03:55] [00:03:55] Audience (Speaker 2): any risk to our fallbacks if the experiment causes higher token churn?
[00:04:02] Jules: our fallback stack is intact: router policy -> model variant -> region failover. we've updated the automatic fallback to prefer the lower-latency variant, and we added more aggressive KV cache priming. still, that's why we need the rollback playbook.
[00:04:18] Samara: walkthrough the rollback playbook in the next section please.
[00:04:25] Jules: sure, short version: 1) metric trigger (p95 latency > SLA threshold for 5 min OR error rate > 0.5%), 2) automatic routing fallback to baseline variant, 3) notify on-call channel and page SRE, 4) open incident ticket and execute canary rollback if needed. We also added a manual override for product owners.
[00:04:49] [00:04:49] Diego: we need to ensure the trace IDs and KV correlation keys are visible to SREs in the first five minutes — make debugging faster.
[00:04:58] Jules: working with observability to add quick filters and dashboards, should be ready prior to canary.
[00:05:08] [00:05:08] Audience (Speaker 3): on security/compliance — will these experiments change data retention or introduce new audit surfaces?
[00:05:16] Samara: short answer: no changes to retention. experiments are computational and routing changes only. any new logs from debugging will be purged per policy; security has signed off on that clause.
[00:05:29] Priya: a small note — the quant eval generates additional intermediate artifacts for analysis, we'll keep those internal and rotate them after 7 days.
[00:05:40] [00:05:40] Maya: switching topics to product milestones: December roadmap is light; main focus is experiments, the public API stability patches, and a small Optimize UI refresh to expose model selection telemetry.
[00:05:56] Samara: can you remind folks of the success criteria for the Optimize UI refresh?
[00:06:01] Maya: sure — primary signal is increased adoption of the suggested batching profile by 20% among heavy customers within two weeks of the UI change, plus reduced average tokens per session for pilot customers.
[00:06:15] [00:06:15] Jules: ops-wise we also want a dashboard to compare model throughput across quant profiles, that's an Eng deliverable.
[00:06:23] Samara: okay let's talk about the holiday on-call schedule briefly — Rohan?
[00:06:28] Rohan: yes, we'll publish the holiday rotation next Monday. main change: more distributed regional overlaps to avoid single-point paging in the EU/East windows. anyone with conflicts please ping People.
[00:06:40] [00:06:40] Audience (Speaker 4): will the rotation increase load for EMEA? we already are stretched.
[00:06:46] Rohan: we aim to balance load by shifting some batch tasks out of the EMEA midnights; it's a temporary bump for some folks. we'll offer time-off swaps and comp days.
[00:06:58] [00:06:58] Diego: quick FYI from infra: a planned kernel optimization landed in a sub-cluster testbed, and we saw a 7% p50 improvement for long sequences, but the p99 effects are not yet stable. We'll coordinate with Research on quant compatibility.
[00:07:15] Priya: that optimization interacts subtly with operator fusion in our runtime; in a couple test cases the quantized path had slightly higher memory pressure. I'm running a two-week internal stress with mixed sequences.
[00:07:29] Maya: how are we measuring the memory spikes — is that observable at tenant granularity?
[00:07:33] Priya: yes, traces include per-tenant mem counters, but we need new tagging to tie it to model variant so we've asked Eng to add that.
[00:07:42] Jules: adding the tags next sprint.
[00:07:45] [00:07:45] Audience (Speaker 5): competitor question — heard GigaCloud rolled out a new managed runtime, worried about price wars — how are we positioned?
[00:07:56] Samara: we expect competitors to tinker with price, but our differentiation is predictable economics + rollout/ops tooling. experiments are about protecting margin while keeping reliability. Diego, words on differentiation?
[00:08:08] Diego: emphasize our model of unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private and the deployment guardrails — that's hard to replicate. pricing moves are noise; customers care about total cost of ownership and SLA.
[00:08:20] [00:08:20] Audience (Speaker 6): question about Dedicated customers and private deployments — are we planning any changes to the private control plane?
[00:08:29] Maya: nothing immediate in December; longer term, Q1 we'll prototype a lighter telemetry option for private that trims telemetry to decrease network egress.
[00:08:39] Samara: ok, and on audits: Security will run a mock SOC review in January to prep for next year's customer audits.
[00:08:46] [00:08:46] Audience (Speaker 7): can we get a brief on experiment transparency — will customers see when they're in an experiment?
[00:08:54] Maya: yes, for any customer exposed in a trial we'll clearly communicate and provide an opt-out path. Dedicated customers never get forced changes.
[00:09:04] Samara: closing notes — timeline recap: experiment A/B/C start next Monday, metrics dashboard by Wednesday, rollback playbook and canary triggers in place by Friday.
[00:09:15] Jules: and I'll circulate the one-page rollback doc and the incident playbook in #ops; please review.
[00:09:19] Samara: final housekeeping: posting all slides and experiment docs to the all-hands folder; Maya please share the experiment spreadsheet link.
[00:09:27] Maya: will do, link will be in #all-hands in 10.
[00:09:31] [00:09:31] Quick pulse: shoutouts — thanks to the infra team for the kernel tweak and to Research for the quant eval runs.
[00:09:40] Audience (Speaker 8): appreciate the transparency — small ask: can we have a short async recap for teams in APAC time zones?
[00:09:48] Rohan: yes, we'll send a summary and record of this and schedule two shorter syncs for APAC windows.
[00:09:56] Samara: great. We're out of time. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
